Getting started with carpeDIAMS

Source: vignettes/carpeDIAMS.Rmd
carpeDIAMS.Rmd
library(carpeDIAMS)

Inputs

carpediams(input, output, targetlist = NULL, ...) picks a route from its input:

input targetlist Route
XcmsExperiment/XCMSnExp, or .rds/.qs/.rda path ignored process_xcms()
mzML file, mzML directory, or vector of paths given process_targetlist()
one mzML file NULL process_mzml()
mzML directory or vector of paths NULL error

Any other argument goes to the routed function, so you can call that function directly instead if you prefer.

xcms object 

carpediams(input = "grouped_xcms.rds", output = "features.mgf",
           top_n = 10, ppm = 20, rt_buffer = 5)

The object must have been through xcms::groupChromPeaks(). Each feature in featureDefinitions() is built from its top_n most intense samples (by featureValues(value = "into")). In each of those samples, the scans come from the feature’s chromatographic peak, widened by rt_buffer seconds. For large cohorts, subsample = TRUE, subset_size = 100 first reduces the samples to a representative set with apricot (Python).

mzML files and a target list 

carpediams(input = "data/mzml/", output = "targets.mgf",
           targetlist = "targets.csv", rt_width = 15, ppm = 20)

The target list needs mz and rt columns, and optionally feature for ids. An rt column whose maximum is below 60 is read as minutes. Every target is extracted from every file, in an rt_width-second window centred on its rt. No peak detection is done.

One mzML file 

carpediams(input = "sample.mzML", output = "sample.mgf")

process_mzml() keeps 30–1200 s (rt_range), runs centWave with fixed parameters, and builds a spectrum for every peak found. Fragments are scored across the scans of that single file. This route accepts only rt_range, grouper, group_statistics_fn and filter_fn.

Defaults

Step Default Change with
Scan window per sample apex = highest MS1 scan; keep scans < 50 scans from it buffer, apex_source, window_mode
m/z grouping ppm_upgma(ppm = 20) (xcms, target list) or ppm_upgma(ppm = 30) (mzML) grouper, ppm
Consensus m/z consensus_mz_weighted(frac = 0.5, Isat = 1e4) consensus_mz_fn
Statistics correlation_statistics(min_count = 10) group_statistics_fn, min_count
Filter correlation_filtering(cor_thresh = 0.1, fdr_thresh = 0.1) filter_fn, cor_thresh, fdr_thresh

buffer, apex_source, window_mode and consensus_mz_fn are passed through ... and work on the xcms and target-list routes only.

The pipeline’s default filter (0.1 / 0.1) is more permissive than the defaults of the correlation_filtering() factory itself (0.3 / 0.01). If you build the filter yourself, set both thresholds explicitly.

Choosing a grouper

All samples’ centroids for a feature are grouped in one call, so the tolerance has to cover both scatter within a sample and calibration drift between samples.

ppm_upgma(ppm = 20)                       # group width <= 20 ppm of the precursor m/z
abs_upgma(max_diff = 0.005)               # group width <= 0.005 Da
iaac_grouper(k = 2, p0 = 12, Isat = 1e4)  # intensity-dependent tolerance
pelt_grouper(p0 = 15, Isat = 1e5)         # optimal partition, same noise model
bin_grouper(bin_width = 0.01)             # fixed bins

iaac_grouper() and pelt_grouper() give each centroid an m/z uncertainty of p0 ppm at high intensity, growing as sqrt(Isat / intensity) below Isat. Weak centroids are therefore allowed to scatter more.

Statistics and filters

For each fragment group, correlation_statistics() sums the fragment intensity per (sample, MS1 scan), correlates those sums with the MS1 intensity, and reports correlation, p_value, BH-adjusted fdr, count (number of cells) and n_samples. Groups need more than min_count cells.

apex_correlation_statistics() also reports how far the fragment’s elution centre is from the precursor’s, in scans (apex_shift_med, apex_shift_iqr across samples). Pair it with apex_correlation_filtering() to reject co-eluting fragments that correlate but peak at the wrong time:

carpediams(
  input = "grouped_xcms.rds", output = "features.mgf",
  group_statistics_fn = apex_correlation_statistics(min_count = 10),
  filter_fn = apex_correlation_filtering(cor_thresh = 0.5, fdr_thresh = 0.01,
                                         max_apex_shift_med = 0.5,
                                         max_apex_shift_iqr = 0.75)
)

A filter is just a function of the statistics table:

carpediams(input = "grouped_xcms.rds", output = "features.mgf",
           filter_fn = function(stats) stats[correlation > 0.6 & count >= 20])

The MGF

Every feature (or target) gets exactly one block, in input order, with TITLE, PEPMASS, RTINSECONDS, CHARGE=1+, MSLEVEL=2 and IONMODE. Peak intensity is the mean, over (sample, scan) cells, of the summed fragment intensity. When no spectrum could be built, the block has no peaks and the title says why:

Title suffix Meaning
DeconvERROR:MissingTargetInfo no precursor m/z (or no RT on the target-list route)
DeconvERROR:MissingMs1Signal no MS1 scans were extracted for the feature
DeconvERROR:NoAssociatedFragments no fragment group passed the statistics and filter

Larger datasets

carpediams() runs everything in one R session by default. The xcms and target-list routes can also run as separate stages (prepare, one sample job per file, filter in batches, finalize) that share a working directory:

  • vignette("xcms-interactive") walks through the stages in R.
  • vignette("dag-cli") covers running them as cluster jobs.
